wa_northwest_face_boving_pollock.notes: A short traverse gains a steep corner system; committing 5.10-ish moves lead to a ledge, where some parties belay while others continue on delicate gear to a small-tree stance protected with pitons and cams.
The right-facing corner above has limited feet and hard-won small gear placements -- the route's technical crux, solid for the grade.
A short chimney leads into a vegetated crack, working past a block to a big ledge belay.
Easier, sometimes-unroped ground heads for the base of the prominent double overhangs above -- the shared Boving Roofs feature.
Climbs over the pair of obvious overhangs with good protection and committing moves, belaying in a gully above -- the Boving Roofs 'money pitch' shared with the Southwest Rib variation.
A nice hand crack past one 5.9-ish move gives way to easier ground on the right, often simul-climbed or scrambled to the top, finishing on the Southwest Rib's upper pitches.
